designs.name: Simple random
designs.definition: Any group of quadrats is equally likely to be chosen as any other. The app draws the quadrat centres uniformly at random across the whole meadow (you may redraw once).
designs.pros: Unbiased for every species; simplest to justify in a report.
designs.cons: Can leave gaps; for species tied to a gradient, plain random samples can be unevenly spread, so estimates vary more between repeats.
designs.expectedBehavior: Approximately unbiased estimate for all species; moderate spread for the gradient species.

designs.name: Systematic (even grid)
designs.definition: Quadrats on a regular grid with a random starting offset — sample at fixed intervals from a random start.
designs.pros: Spreads quadrats evenly over the meadow; easy to walk; usually steadier (less spread between repeats) than simple random.
designs.cons: If the meadow's pattern has a matching rhythm, a grid can align with it badly; one random start only.
learnerControls: the grid start is randomised once
designs.expectedBehavior: Approximately unbiased; usually lower spread than simple random for the clumped and gradient species.

designs.name: Stratified by moisture zone
designs.definition: Divide the meadow into equal-area strata (wet, mid, dry thirds along the moisture gradient), then place the same number of quadrats at random within each stratum.
designs.pros: Guarantees the wet ground is sampled — best when you already know a gradient matters (the map shows the zones before you choose).
designs.cons: Requires knowing the strata in advance; slightly more walking.
learnerControls: zones are shown on the map
designs.expectedBehavior: Approximately unbiased; lowest spread for the moisture-gradient species (Blue Sedge).

designs.name: Wherever looks interesting
designs.definition: A non-probability design: you place each quadrat wherever looks interesting — typically right where the showy plants catch your eye. Nothing is wrong with curiosity, but this is convenience sampling, and it is not a fair sample of the meadow.
designs.pros: Feels efficient; you see lots of the showy species up close.
designs.cons: You choose where to sample, so some parts of the meadow become far more likely than others — exactly what sampling bias is.
learnerControls: click or keyboard-place each quadrat anywhere on the map
designs.expectedBehavior: Deliberately biased upward for the showy clumped species (Butterweed) and almost blind to the rare Fen Orchid. The reveal and the re-sampling simulator make this visible.
